channel.title: The Polymath Dispatch
channel.description: A daily journal of history and philosophy.

item.title: Epictetus in the Laboratory of Modernity: Psychotherapy, Survival, and Quietism
item.description: From the birth of cognitive behavioural therapy to Hanoi prison cells and modern political critiques, Epictetus’s radical ethics faces its ultimate trial.

item.title: The Triadic Soul: Epictetus on Desire, Action, and Assent
item.description: Epictetus transforms Stoic theory into an actionable psychological curriculum for mastering human consciousness.

item.title: The Inner Citadel: Epictetus on Moral Volition and the Bounds of Control
item.description: An exploration of why our judgments are our sole domain, and how ancient Stoic volition preserves human dignity against circumstance.

item.title: The Slave Who Rebuilt Freedom: Epictetus and Stoic Inner Sovereignty
item.description: How an enslaved Greek in Nero's Rome transformed personal subjection into the ancient world's most radical philosophy of inner freedom.

item.title: The Architecture of the Prehistoric Mind: Synthesis and Debates in Indian Antiquity
item.description: How non-literate societies engineered social hierarchy, ritual soundscapes, and regional networks across ancient South Asia before the urban dawn.

item.title: Between Flint and Furnace: The Chalcolithic Villages of Peninsular India
item.description: Beyond the shadow of the Indus cities, farming communities across Rajasthan, Malwa, and the Deccan forged an enduring rural order in painted clay and hammered copper.

item.title: The Sedentary Revolution: How Mehrgarh Anchored Ancient South Asia
item.description: At the foot of the Bolan Pass, seven thousand years ago, early South Asians abandoned mobile foraging to build mud-brick granaries, domesticate Zebu cattle, and pave the way for urban civilization.

item.title: Stone and Shadow: Palaeolithic and Mesolithic Life at Bhimbetka
item.description: How seven hundred sandstone shelters in central India preserved a hundred-thousand-year ledger of human technology, art, and spiritual consciousness.

item.title: Reading the Silent Earth: How Archaeologists Date and Interpret Prehistoric India
item.description: Before kings, inscriptions, and sacred hymns, material stones and buried isotopes establish the chronological architecture of the Indian subcontinent.

item.title: The Shadow of the Purple: Criticisms, Legacy, and Modern Stoicism
item.description: Examining the gap between Marcus Aurelius's philosophical ideals, his imperial realities, and his turbulent modern afterlife.

item.title: The Architecture of the Self: Marcus Aurelius and Stoic Spiritual Exercises
item.description: How a Roman emperor used rigorous mental disciplines to protect his ruling faculty and serve the common good amidst war and plague.

item.title: The Emperor's Midnight Mirror: Reading the Meditations as Living Physics
item.description: Marcus Aurelius wrote not for posterity but to discipline his own soul through the rational architecture of the cosmos.

item.title: The Reluctant Sovereign: Duty, Plague, and War in Antonine Rome
item.description: How Marcus Aurelius forged enduring Stoic wisdom amidst devastating pestilence and border warfare on the Danube frontier.
